data.title: US STOCKS-Nasdaq rebounds as chip stocks recover from steep losses
data.description:
* Indexes: Dow flat, S&P 500 0.94%, Nasdaq 1.71%

* Airbnb ( ABNB ) jumps after raising FY revenue growth forecast

* October nonfarm payrolls at +165,000 vs 65,000 estimate

(Updates to afternoon trading levels, adds analyst comments)

By Shashwat Chauhan and Utkarsh Hathi

Nov 6 (Reuters) - The tech-heavy Nasdaq rose on Friday as chip stocks bounced off heavy losses posted in the previous session on fears that a Democrats-led Congress could result in tougher AI regulation, even as the jobs report raised interest-rate hike concerns.

The Nasdaq Composite logged its steepest one-day decline in 19 months on Thursday, confirming it had entered correction territory. The index was also headed for a fourth straight weekly decline.

The selloff followed the Democrats' midterm election victory, including in key data-center states, stoking concerns that AI data-center buildout could slow. Optimism over the sector's rapid growth had propelled stock markets to record highs this year.

"It's just that yesterday's reaction seemed pretty pronounced and people are kind of just stepping in a bit," said Thomas Shipp, vice president of equity research at LPL Financial.

Megacap and growth stocks were mixed. Nvidia ( NVDA ) added 3.8%, after suffering its worst day since January 2025 when the emergence of low-cost Chinese AI model DeepSeek had rattled Wall Street.

Chip stocks staged a recovery, with the broader semiconductor index rising 4.2%, after plunging over 12% in the previous session. AMD, Intel ( INTC ) and Micron Technology ( MU ) were up between 6% and 10%.

Meanwhile, US nonfarm payrolls increased more than expected in October and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, suggesting the labor market remained resilient.

Traders added to bets that the Fed could hike rates as soon as next month, with a 78% chance of a December move compared with a 70% chance seen earlier.

"Those are strong numbers ... the flip side is what we saw yesterday and how volatility has spiked; will the Fed want to raise interest rates in the face of a market which is teetering?" said Joe Saluzzi, co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading.

At 11:31 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average held steady at 51,555 points, the S&P 500 gained 69.32 points, or 0.94%, to 7,423.05 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 415.39 points, or 1.71%, to 24,730.30.

Six of the 11 S&P 500 sectors were trading higher, with information technology leading gains. Consumer staples and healthcare were the laggards.

The benchmark was on pace for its worst week since June.

Data-center operators IREN ( IREN ) and Applied Digital ( APLD ) , neoclouds CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius Group ( NBIS ) and AI-exposed utilities and equipment suppliers such as GE Vernova ( GEV ) and Constellation Energy ( CEG ) recovered from deep losses in the last session.

Elon Musk-led Tesla and SpaceX were also up 5% and 6%, respectively, after dropping sharply in the last two sessions.

Bucking the trend, Microchip slid 12.1% and was heading for its steepest weekly fall since December 2000, after the chip supplier forecast third-quarter adjusted gross margin below estimates.

A jump in crude oil prices on Thursday had also pressured equities over concerns of energy-fueled inflation and prospects of higher interest rates by global central banks. Brent crude futures were slightly lower on Friday.

Among other stock movers, software firm Atlassian ( TEAM ) dropped 15.4% after reporting first-quarter results. Airbnb ( ABNB ) climbed 10.4% after the vacation rental platform raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth forecast.

(Reporting by Shashwat Chauhan and Utkarsh Hathi in Bengaluru; Editing by Saumyadeb Chakrabarty, Arun Koyyur and Joyjeet Das)

data.title: US job growth surges in October; unemployment rate falls to 4.1%
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 6 (Reuters) - US job growth accelerated in October and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, suggesting that the labor market could be strengthening after stumbling in mid-summer and keeping the Federal Reserve on track to raise interest rates in December.

The Labor Department's closely watched employment report on Friday also showed the economy added 84,000 more jobs in August and September than previously reported. The decline in the unemployment rate from 4.2% in September was despite 421,000 people entering the labor force.

The better-than-expected report followed on the heels of data this week showing a rise in job openings in September, which combined with historically low layoffs has raised the specter of the labor market tightening. Economists and US central bank officials have maintained that the labor market poses no inflation risk.

"The economy is either at or very near full employment," said Carl Weinberg, chief economist at High Frequency Economics. "We expect the Fed to pivot to focus on the risk of labor demand exceeding labor supply at current levels of demand growth."

Nonfarm payrolls jumped by 165,000 jobs last month after an upwardly revised 60,000 gain in September, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast payrolls advancing 65,000 after a previously reported 29,000 increase in September.

Estimates ranged from 35,000 to 125,000 jobs. August's employment gains were revised up to 186,000 from the previously estimated 133,000. Last month's broad-based increase in payrolls was led by the professional and business services industry, which added 70,000 jobs, well above the average monthly gain of 15,000 over the past 12 months.

Healthcare employment increased by 42,000 jobs, while the transportation and warehousing sector added 25,000 positions.

Manufacturing payrolls rose by 19,000 jobs, spread across computer and electronic products, machinery and primary metals. The increases are likely linked to the artificial intelligence buildout. There were modest job gains in the retail, financial activities and government sectors.

CONSTRUCTION SHEDS JOBS

Construction shed 3,000 jobs while leisure and hospitality employment dropped by 13,000 positions.

The share of industries reporting growth last month increased to 57.6% from 54.2% in September.

Financial markets priced in a roughly 76.8% chance of a rate hike at the US central bank's meeting next month, up from 66.9% on Thursday, CME's FedWatch tool showed.

The Fed last week left its benchmark overnight interest rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range. Next Tuesday's consumer inflation report for October could offer more clues on the course of monetary policy in early 2027. The dollar advanced against a basket of currencies. US Treasury yields rose.

Economists estimate the economy needs to create at least 40,000 jobs per month to keep up with growth in the working-age population. The so-called breakeven rate has declined from roughly 150,000 in 2024 because of the smaller labor force.

The unemployment rate declined from 4.2% in September. Household employment, a volatile measure, increased 463,000 in October, more than enough to absorb the people who entered the labor force. But more people worked part-time for economic reasons last month, with the number increasing 339,000 to 4.840 million. Many unemployed also experienced long bouts of joblessness.

Despite the surge in payrolls, employment gains are lagging economic growth, with gross domestic product increasing at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter, fueled by strong consumer spending and businesses aggressively investing in AI.

Economists said employers likely overhired after the COVID pandemic, and some businesses were probably uncertain about their staffing needs as they incorporated AI into their operations. They said uncertainty stemming from the US-Israeli war with Iran, which has raised energy prices, was also making employers hesitant to increase headcount.

Wage growth maintained its moderate pace, which economists said was a sign that the labor market was not tightening and was not a source of inflation. Wages increased 3.1% in the 12 months through October after rising 3.2% in September. The average workweek was unchanged at 34.4 hours.

​

(Reporting by Lucia Mutikani; Editing by Chizu Nomiyama and Andrea Ricci )

data.title: Under Armour Cuts Full-Year Gross Margin Outlook Amid Freight Cost Headwinds
data.description:
12:22 PM EST, 11/06/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Under Armour ( UAA ) trimmed its full-year gross margin guidance Friday as higher freight costs and planned inventory markdowns are expected to weigh on profitability.

The sportswear maker now expects fiscal 2027 gross margin to expand 170 to 220 basis points, down from its previous outlook of 220 to 270 basis points.

"A 50-basis-point reduction in our gross margin outlook reflects ongoing elevated fuel and freight costs, planned markdowns to improve inventory alignment and a stronger US dollar," Chief Financial Officer Reza Taleghani said during an earnings conference call Friday, according to a FactSet transcript.

Under Armour's ( UAA ) class A shares declined 2% during Friday trading, while class C shares fell 1.5%.

The company now expects headwinds from the Middle East conflict of about $45 million, up from the $35 million previously projected. Its earlier outlook assumed the Middle East disruption would last through September, Taleghani said.

The US-Israel-Iran war has lasted more than eight months now.

Under Armour's ( UAA ) gross margin guidance includes a 150-basis-point tailwind from tariff recoveries.

The company said it will align inventory with demand conditions.

Under Armour ( UAA ) continues to expect a mid-single-percentage-digit revenue decline in fiscal 2027 and adjusted earnings per share of $0.08 to $0.12. Analysts polled by FactSet expect revenue of $4.73 billion -- a 4.9% year-over-year drop -- and non-GAAP EPS of $0.11.

For the quarter ended Sept. 30, Under Armour's ( UAA ) revenue declined 7% to $1.24 billion, exceeding analysts' estimate of $1.23 billion. The company broke even versus $0.04 in adjusted EPS a year ago. The market expected a loss of $0.01 per share.

Last month, UBS Securities expected Under Armour's ( UAA ) second-quarter adjusted EPS broadly in-line, supported by tariff tailwinds and cost actions. The brokerage at the time said that the company's innovation pipeline would help it deliver stronger-than-expected revenue growth as macro challenges ease.

Sales in North America dropped 6.9%, while Europe, the Middle East, and Africa fell 8.5%. Asia Pacific declined 8.8%, while Latin America was the sole region with growth, at 3%.

Wholesale revenue slipped 6.5% to $725 million, while direct-to-consumer sales were off 8.2% to nearly $493.9 million. Apparel, footwear and accessories declined.

For the ongoing quarter, Under Armour ( UAA ) expects revenue to decline about 8% to 9% and an adjusted loss of $0.01 to $0.03 per share. The market forecasts non-GAAP EPS of $0.04 on an expected 4.6% sales drop.

Footwear maker Crocs ( CROX ) late last month raised its full-year outlook after reporting better-than-expected third-quarter results amid broad-based business strength.

Also in October, Nike ( NKE ) said it expected revenue to decline in the high-single-digit range for fiscal 2027.

data.title: Tesla to pull the plug on Cybertruck after years of poor sales
data.description:
Nov 6 (Reuters) - Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around mid-2027, CEO Elon Musk said on Friday, after years of persistently weak sales for a futuristic model once touted as a rival to legacy pickup trucks.

Musk said in an X post the production wind-down would enable the automaker to accommodate increased output of its newly launched Cybercab model, which the billionaire has made central to Tesla's robotaxi ambitions.

The announcement comes at the end of a bruising week for Musk as his record political spending of nearly half a billion dollars yielded little in Tuesday's US midterm elections, with the vast majority of the Republican candidates he backed losing their races.

Combined, his companies were on track to lose more than $370 billion in market capitalization for the week.

While it was not immediately clear whether Cybertruck production would be moved to another facility or phased out entirely, the automaker's Austin plant is the only known Tesla facility equipped to manufacture the specialized components for the heavy, angular model.

In response to a user on X, Musk called the Cybertruck the "best vehicle Tesla has ever made" and the wind-down the "end of an era."

Tesla did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment sent outside regular business hours.

The US electric vehicle maker began delivering the Cybertruck to customers in late 2023. According to automotive data platform Kelley Blue Book, the company only sold 20,237 Cybertrucks in the US last year, down 48% from 38,965 in 2024. Around the start of production in 2023, Musk had predicted annual sales of 250,000 units.

"It doesn't make sense to keep it going when it's not meeting its targets," said former Aston Martin CEO Andy Palmer. "Every rational auto guy would say the same."

"It will no doubt only be a rounding error on Tesla's balance sheet, but the statistics speak for themselves."

Musk's SpaceX was one of the model's biggest customers last year and bought Cybertrucks worth $131 million from Tesla in 2025 at list price, according to its IPO filing.

'CYBERTRUCK WON'T GO, CAN'T GO'

Right from its unveiling in 2019, the Cybertruck was a controversial choice for Musk. Pickup truck purists mocked its angular design, and safety experts predicted it would be hard to gain approval for sale in key markets like Europe.

The unveiling event itself was marred when Musk tried to prove that its windows were shatterproof by having metal balls thrown at them - only to leave massive cracks in two of them.

During Cybertruck's official launch in 2023, Musk touted it as a futuristic competitor to pickup trucks from General Motors and Ford, saying "finally, the future will look like the future."

But the model has struggled to meet those expectations. Tesla has issued 11 recalls for the Cybertruck since it went on sale in late 2023, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. Some vehicles required physical repairs, while others were fixed with over-the-air software updates.

Automotive analyst Felipe Munoz said that although the Cybertruck has been called a failure because of its poor sales, electric pickups from Ford and others have also flopped in the US market.

"All of them lost the competition because electric pick ups aren't popular in the US," Munoz said.

But Cybertruck's sharp-edged stainless-steel design limited its prospects in markets like Europe where EVs are more popular. Regulatory approval was impossible for Europe because of rules there concerning pedestrian impact.

"Anywhere where you have crash regulation that takes into account pedestrian impact, that Cybertruck won't go, can't go," former Aston Martin CEO Palmer said.

MUSK'S NEW BET

The Cybercab, which has butterfly doors and no steering wheel, pedals or mirrors, is one of Musk's key bets in his push to turn Tesla into an AI and robotics company rather than just an automaker.

Musk has said he sees it as Tesla's main autonomous model supplying a global network of robotaxis.

After years of delays to Musk's self-driving targets, Tesla began offering paid rides in a small fleet of Cybercabs in Austin in September. However, the automaker still has to answer the US auto safety agency's questions on whether it has properly self-certified Cybercab to demonstrate compliance with federal motor vehicle safety standards.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an audit in September to review the basis for that certification.

"Cybertruck was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab," Cybertruck lead engineer Wes Morrill said on X.

However, the Cybercab is unlikely to make up for lost Cybertruck volumes soon. The two-seater robotaxi is still a small program, with production beginning only earlier this year. Tesla has listed an installed capacity of more than 125,000 units.

About 570 of the more than 1,200 Tesla robotaxis operating in Texas are Cybercabs, with the rest mainly Model Y vehicles, according to the state's Department of Motor Vehicles.

(Reporting by Ananya Palyekar, Akanksha Khushi and Akash Sriram in Bengaluru; Editing by Jochelle Mendonca, Janane Venkatraman, Raju Gopalakrishnan and Jonathan Ananda)

data.title: For clean windows, just press a button
data.description:
BEIJING, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The following article was published today by China Daily.

There is good news for those who dread cleaning windows. There are robots out there to take on the tedious and sometimes dangerous task, and do a good job of it.

Ask Liang Yu. The 55-year-old resident of Guangzhou, Guangdong province, bought a window-cleaning robot for her 11th-floor apartment. Its performance was so impressive that she bought another one for her mother-in-law.

It was a welcome alternative to a chore she once tackled or paid someone to do. To get started, Liang fills the robot's water inlet with solution, plugs in the power cord and secures the robot's safety tether beside the window. Then she presses a button.

The device, fitted with two discs covered in cleaning pads, clings to the outside of the window and works its way across the glass.

"It's a wonderful invention and checks all my boxes. I can clean the windows whenever I want," said Liang, a businesswoman.

Initially, Liang was hesitant to buy the robot due to safety concerns. However, after watching livestream demonstrations, she paid about 1,200 yuan ($180) in a promotional sale last year and got one for herself.

According to AVC, a home appliances market consultancy, China's window-cleaning robot market expanded from 480 million yuan in 2020 to 1.7 billion yuan in 2025.

Chinese window-cleaning robots are drawing attention abroad as well.

On Amazon.com, a Canadian consumer commented that "I don't take pleasure in cleaning, so I really like this robot as it reduces the amount of effort for me. ... Just plop it on a window as you take care of other cleaning tasks."

At the recent 140th China Import and Export Fair, or Canton Fair, in Guangzhou, window-cleaning robots made by Chinese companies drew crowds of potential overseas buyers.

One such manufacturer is Shanxi Jiashida Robot Technology. Established in 2012, the company exports its products to 56 countries and regions, including the United States, Germany and Japan, with Europe being its main market.

Feng Fenfen, head of the company's foreign trade department, said that customers at home and abroad want effective cleaning at a good price, while overseas buyers place more emphasis on safety and environmental protection.

The company's product has a dual-disc design, with each disc acting as a suction cup while fitted with a cleaning pad. The discs work alternately, with one holding against the glass while the other moves. Autonomous path-planning technology helps the robot identify edges and adjust its cleaning operation.

Feng said the company has adapted its products for different markets. The suction system is adjusted to deal with extreme cold climates, while in areas prone to sand and grit, a dedicated model is designed to remove these particles prior to washing.

Niu Liqun, chairman of the company, said the company will keep using real scenarios to drive its technology development.

The industry is also moving toward consistent performance benchmarks, with China's first household window-cleaning robots standard set to take effect on Dec 1. It sets unified threshold requirements and criteria.

Chinese manufacturers such as Ecovacs and Dreame Technology are also integrating algorithms into their window-cleaning robots.

Wei Wei, deputy dean of the School of Computer and Information Technology at Shanxi University, said: "With breakthroughs in multimodal perception, intelligent decision-making and large model technologies, window-cleaning robots are evolving from automated devices into intelligent autonomous machines."

For robot users, a chore that once required effort, expense and planning now begins with a button.

data.title: CANADA STOCKS-Healthcare, tech push TSX higher; jobless rate at six-month high
data.description:
By Anand Gopal R

Nov 6 (Reuters) - Canada's main stock index inched higher on Friday as healthcare and technology stocks offset losses in industrials, while investors digested data showing the domestic unemployment rate hit a six-month high in October.

The S&P/TSX Composite Index rose 0.45% to 35,766.11 points as of 11:11 a.m. ET (1611 GMT).

* The Canadian economy shed a net 4,700 jobs in October, data showed, as the private sector and full-time employment both declined, pushing the unemployment rate to a six-month high

* Defensive healthcare stocks led the gains, rising 1.5%, while industrials declined 0.6%

* Technology stocks advanced 0.8%, rebounding from a 3.8% drop in the prior session driven by a selloff in US AI shares

* Fears of tighter US AI regulation continue to weigh on sentiment, after wiping trillions off global equities and fuelling a rush into safe-haven bonds

* Yields in the benchmark Canadian 10-year bonds fell around 2 basis points to 3.647%

* The energy sector index rose 0.8% and was set to snap a two-day losing streak

* Meanwhile, in the US, job growth accelerated in October and unemployment fell to 4.1%, reinforcing expectations of a December rate hike by the Federal Reserve

* Traders also parsed Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney's second budget, which plans to tap windfall oil revenues to boost productivity and infrastructure while keeping fiscal targets intact and reducing reliance on the US

* Still, there could be "a positive shift for US-Canadian relations," said Michael J. Constantino, CEO of Webull Canada, pointing to the Democrats' control of Congress, which could ease trade and diplomatic frictions

data.title: Facility Grid Appoints Five-Time Software CEO Tim Curran to Board of Directors
data.description:
Construction and real estate technology veteran joins as Facility Grid builds the unified building lifecycle platform.

BROOKLINE, Mass.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Facility Grid, a Nexa Equity portfolio company and a leading provider of cloud-based commissioning (Cx), operational readiness (OR), and sustainability software for the construction industry, today announced the appointment of Tim Curran to its Board of Directors.

The appointment comes as Facility Grid expands from a market-leading commissioning platform into a unified building lifecycle software company. Following its acquisition of PingCx in August, Facility Grid now offers three integrated products on one AI-enabled platform: FG Construct for commissioning, quality management, and operational readiness; FG Validate for autonomous building systems testing; and FG Sustain for energy audits, carbon reporting, and ongoing building performance.

“Our goal is to become the system of record for engineering across the full building lifecycle, from construction through operations,” said Daniel Russo, CEO of Facility Grid. “Tim has built and scaled market-defining companies on both sides of that lifecycle, and we worked together at Building Engines. His experience will help us sharpen our strategy and grow faster.”

A five-time software CEO, Curran has spent 20 years in construction and real estate technology. He led Vela Systems, the construction industry’s first mobile field management software, through its 2012 acquisition by Autodesk, where it became BIM 360. He later led Building Engines, the commercial real estate operations platform acquired by JLL in 2021, and earlier led Eleven Technology through its 2006 acquisition by Trimble. Curran is Executive Chairman of Rapidworks, which offers quote-to-cash and operation management solutions to heavy equipment trade contractors, and a Board Director of Knowify, which offers cloud-based project and service management software for the construction trades. He also advises and invests in more than a dozen vertical SaaS companies.

“The industry still manages buildings through disconnected point solutions, and the data breaks at every handoff, especially at turnover,” said Curran. “Facility Grid is connecting the data from construction through operations, which is where the real value is. I’m excited to help Daniel and the team accelerate that vision.”

About Facility Grid

Facility Grid is the AI-enabled Lifecycle Commissioning® platform for construction quality, autonomous testing, and sustainability, from preconstruction through ongoing operations. Its FG Construct, FG Validate, and FG Sustain products help commissioning providers, data centers, contractors, quality teams, and building owners verify quality at the point of work, reduce rework, and deliver operational readiness and lasting building performance. For more information, visit www.facilitygrid.com.

data.title: European Stocks Tumble in Friday Trading; Bank of England Raises Rates for First Time Since 2023
data.description:
11:45 AM EST, 11/06/2026 (MT Newswires) -- The stock markets closed sharply lower in Friday trading after the Bank of England raised its key policy rate Thursday by 25 basis points to 4%. It was the first time the Bank raised rates in more than three years.

The Stoxx Europe lost 1.2%, Germany's DAX shed 2.1%, the FTSE 100 dropped 1%, France's CAC declined 0.9%, and the Swiss Market Index decreased 1.3%.

The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee voted 8-1 to raise the Bank Rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4%. One member voted for a 0.5 percentage point increase to 4.25%.

"The degree of inflationary pressure in the pipeline is now sufficient to warrant an increase in Bank Rate," the Bank said in a statement. "Activity data in recent months have generally been stronger than expected, adding to the case for modestly tighter monetary policy."

In corporate news, Novartis said testing has linked two tumor cases to its Zolgensma gene therapy, which treats spinal muscular atrophy, a rare genetic disease that causes progressive muscle weakness, Bloomberg reported Friday.

Since its approval in 2019, nine tumor cases have been reported in patients treated with Zolgensma, the report said. Novartis told Bloomberg it continues to monitor safety reports and assess all reported cases, though it has not confirmed the type or location of the tumors.

The drug's existing safety information warns of a potential tumor risk associated with the therapy's insertion into patients' DNA, Bloomberg reported.

In a statement, Novartis said that more than 6,000 patients have been treated with Zolgensma in various clinical trials, other programs, and commercial treatment, of which the company has received nine reports of tumors, with two showing evidnece of being linked to the drug.

"The patients underwent treatment and continue to be monitored," the company said. "The potential risk of tumors due to vector integration is currently included in the Zolgensma prescribing information."

Shares of the company declined 0.9% in Zurich.

ING Group is offering a portfolio of data center loans worth roughly $500 million for sale through a so-called bids-wanted-in-competition process, Bloomberg reported Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.

The loans for sale include a $25 million portion backing a large data center site in New Mexico that is part of the $500 billion Stargate project, a joint AI infrastructure venture involving OpenAI, SoftBank and Oracle, the report said.

The Dutch bank is also seeking to offload debt linked to operators such as Vantage Data Centers and CyrusOne.

ING did not immediately respond to MT Newswires' request for comment.

Shares of ING fell 1.7% in Amsterdam.

Ascendis Pharma said Friday that the European Medicines Agency's Committee for Orphan Medicinal Products recommended maintaining orphan medicinal product designation for once-weekly TransCon CNP for the treatment of achondroplasia in children.

If TransCon CNP receives marketing authorization in the European Union, the orphan designation would provide 10 years of market exclusivity, the biopharmaceutical company said.

The European Commission's final decision on Ascendis' marketing authorization application is expected in the fourth quarter.

Shares of Ascendis Pharma lost 1.8% in Frankfurt.

data.title: Northern Trust Pension Universe Data: Canadian Pension Plans Navigate Challenging Markets in Q3
data.description:
TORONTO--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Canadian pension plan returns fell in the third quarter, mostly a result of rising bond yields, with the median pension plan returning -1.5% for the quarter ending September 30 and 4.4% year-to-date, according to the Northern Trust Canada Universe.

Third-quarter financial markets were shaped by the return of energy-driven inflation and a sharp rise in global interest rates. Middle East tensions returned to the foreground, pushing Brent crude oil above $100 per barrel and renewing concerns around inflation and energy supply. The rise in oil occurred against a backdrop of resilient economic activity and generally constructive corporate earnings. After holding rates in July, the U.S. Federal Reserve raised its policy rate by 25 basis points in September. The European Central Bank and Bank of Japan also adjusted policy rates higher during the month, while the Bank of Canada and Bank of England maintained their policy rates throughout the quarter. Meanwhile, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield rose more than 80 basis points to 5.29%, while sovereign yields also moved materially higher in Europe, the U.K. and Japan.

Despite this challenging backdrop, global equities, as measured by the MSCI ACWI Index, rose 1.8% in CAD (1.7% in USD) during the third quarter. Strong corporate earnings and resilient economic growth supported markets, while continued investment in artificial intelligence (AI) remained an important driver of sentiment.

“Canadian pension plans navigated a complex market environment in the third quarter, as resilient equity markets were offset by the impact of rising bond yields,” said Katie Pries, Country Executive for Northern Trust Asset Servicing in Canada. “The quarter underscores how shifts in interest rates and inflation expectations can meaningfully influence pension portfolio performance, reinforcing the importance of maintaining a long-term perspective through changing market conditions.”

The Northern Trust Canada Universe tracks the performance of Canadian institutional defined benefit plans that subscribe to performance measurement services as part of Northern Trust’s asset servicing offerings.

In equity markets, U.S. stocks advanced on robust earnings and ongoing AI-related spending, while Japanese equities were among the strongest performers, benefiting from earnings growth and corporate governance reforms. Emerging markets lagged developed markets as semiconductor and memory-related stocks in Korea weakened following strong first-half gains. European equities underperformed amid weaker earnings momentum and higher interest rates, while UK equities benefited from greater exposure to energy and financials sectors.

Global bonds, as represented by the Bloomberg Global Aggregate Index, fell -2.4% in CAD (-2.5% in USD) during the quarter as resilient economic activity, rising energy prices and persistent inflation concerns pushed bond yields higher across most developed markets. Markets also adjusted to expectations for further policy tightening, while increased sovereign issuance and corporate borrowing contributed to upward pressure on yields. Longer-dated government bonds underperformed as yields rose, while investment grade credit generated negative returns despite generally resilient corporate fundamentals. High yield bonds were down globally but proved relatively resilient, supported by higher income and lower interest-rate sensitivity.

  • Canadian equities, as represented by the S&P/TSX Composite Index, returned 1.6% in CAD (1.5% in USD) during the third quarter. Headline inflation was 3.1% at September quarter-end, up from 3.0% the prior month, remaining below the recent peak of 3.2%.
  • U.S. equities, as measured by the S&P 500 Index, gained 2.4% in CAD (2.3% in USD) against a backdrop of higher energy prices, rising yields and uncertainty regarding inflation.
  • International equity markets, as measured by the MSCI EAFE Index, had a gross return of 0.9% in CAD (0.9% in USD) in Q3.
  • During the third quarter, emerging markets (“EM”), as measured by the MSCI EM Index, had a gross decline of -0.2% in CAD (-0.2% in USD).

Canada’s economy showed more resilience than anticipated, yet inflation concerns and higher global bond yields gained prominence by September as trade tensions with the U.S. intensified. The Bank of Canada maintained its policy rate throughout the quarter, balancing largely contained inflation against uncertainty in the outlook arising from trade disputes. The main inflation risks now stem from supply conditions. Higher energy costs and additional tariffs, alongside potential disruptions to global supply chains, could lift prices temporarily across certain sectors.

The Canadian fixed income market, as measured by the FTSE Canada Universe Bond Index, fell -3.0% in CAD (-3.0% in USD). Provincial Bonds fell -4.1% while Federal and Corporate Bonds fell -2.6% and -2.1% respectively. Performance weakened with duration, as Short-, Mid- and Long-term bonds returned -0.9%, -3.0%, and -6.3%, respectively.

U.S. equity performance was largely driven by the energy sector as oil and gas prices surged over global supply concerns following escalating conflict in the Middle East. Information technology also benefitted owing to a shift from semiconductors to software and hyperscalers. As was widely anticipated, the Federal Reserve (“Fed”) unanimously voted to increase its key rate for the first time since July 2023 by 25 basis points, bringing it to a 3.75%-4% range, to tackle inflation brought on by rising oil and gasoline prices owing to the geopolitical conflict in the Middle East. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh noted that while the economy, including the labour market, was strong, inflation had been “too high…for too long”, stating that the rate hike would support a “timelier return” to the bank’s 2 percent target. The dot-plot of officials’ expectations pointed to another 25bps rate hike this year, with some participants seeing the possibility for two. The inflation rate rose to 3.7% in September, up from 3.4% in each of the previous two months and above the expected 3.6% largely resulting from higher energy prices.

The European Central Bank (“ECB”) raised its rates by a quarter point, lifting the deposit rate to 2.5%, its second hike since June, citing inflationary pressures, largely driven by higher oil and gas prices because of renewed fighting around the Strait of Hormuz, constraining crude supply. The bank expressed concern that the surge could translate into higher transport costs and costly heating for properties and noted that food inflation was also likely to rise. The bank also raised its forecast for eurozone growth from 0.8% to 0.9% in 2026. For the sixth time in a row, the Bank of England (“BoE”) held rates steady at 3.75%, in September, as a surge in energy prices pressures inflation. The BoE did however note that it would raise rates if high energy prices persist. The bank also raised its forecast for inflation, stating it would be “slightly above 4%” starting next year. The Bank of Japan raised its interest rates in September to 1.25%, the highest level in 31 years, in an effort to contain inflation resulting from rising energy costs. Governor Ueda noted that the bank’s focus has shifted to guarding against an inflation overshoot as domestic inflation exceeds the 2% target.

Emerging markets produced mixed results during the quarter. The People’s Bank of China left its one- and five-year loan prime rate (LPR) at 3.0% and 3.5%, respectively, for the 16th straight month reflecting caution amid Middle East-related uncertainty. Industrial production strengthened; export activity remained supported by AI-demand while retail sales softened. The Central Bank of Brazil cut its rate to 13.75% noting an uncertain environment due to conflict in the Middle East and monetary policy decisions in advanced economies while domestically data showed a moderation in economic activity and an ease in inflation. The Reserve Bank of India held rates at 5.25%, balancing resilient domestic growth against evolving inflationary and global risks.

data.title: Create With Us: On Tour - Fujifilm Brings Its Flagship Community Event to Creators Nationwide
data.description:
Interactive event goes on tour to connect local creative communities through workshops, experiences, demos, and more

VALHALLA, N.Y.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- FUJIFILM North America Corporation, Electronic Imaging Division, announces the upcoming Create With Us: On Tour, bringing its flagship community event to cities across the country. Running from late 2026 into 2027, the tour gives Fujifilm’s focused demographics - traditional photographers, new users, creators, and cinematographers - the opportunity to develop their skills and connect with fellow creatives from their community.

Create With Us began in Seattle in 2023, welcoming 540 creators through the doors of the iconic Fremont Studios. The event continued in Austin for 2024, followed by Minneapolis the following year. Now, Fujifilm is building on that success with a nationwide tour, working with local camera dealers and primary partner Godox to deliver the event to more creators across the United States.

Each stop on the tour will offer something a little different, shaped by the local creative community. Planned activations include Hands-On Demo stations, where attendees can explore Fujifilm cameras and lenses, guided photowalks, sponsor-led product demos, workshops led by experienced industry professionals, and a networking meetup to finish out the day.

Godox will join Create With Us: On Tour as a lead partner, bringing its expertise in photographic lighting all around the country. Through dedicated classes, industry professional Brent Eysler will share insights drawn from his experience in portraiture, photojournalism, and cinematography. Visitors can also explore techniques in a more practical setting, with lighting photowalks and live equipment demonstrations providing the chance to see Godox equipment in action.

The tour kicks off on December 5, 2026, with dealer partner Competitive Cameras, at Deep Ellum Art Co. in Dallas, Texas, before heading to Miami, Florida on January 16th, with dealer partner AVC Photo Video Store. These two events mark the beginning of a wider schedule, with more destinations to be announced in the future.

By taking the event beyond its previous host cities, Fujifilm aims to build a wider network of creators who can share their knowledge and grow by connecting inside their communities. Over time, this effect can compound and grow arts community groups, as seen at Fujifilm’s national event Fujikina, that took place in SoHo, New York during October 2026.

Create With Us: On Tour is free to attend and open to photographers and filmmakers of all experience levels, from those developing their skills to veteran creators. Attendees can bring their own camera equipment or try Fujifilm gear. While walk-ins are welcome, advanced registration through a local dealer is recommended.

data.title: Big Tech set to drive US corporate bond sales to annual record high, data shows
data.description:
* Hyperscalers raised over $370.7 bln, about a fifth of the total

* Amazon ( AMZN ), Alphabet raised most money from bond sales

* Bond issuance to fund about 35% of hyperscalers' capex in 2027 - Goldman

By Shashwat Chauhan

Nov 6 (Reuters) - US investment-grade corporate bond issuance climbed to $1.88 trillion this year, LSEG data showed, surpassing the previous annual record as Big Tech companies borrow heavily to fund their AI ambitions.

The debt issuance this year through November 4 has already breached the previous record of $1.86 trillion raised in 2020 when companies stockpiled cash during the COVID-19 pandemic, driven by near-zero interest rates.

However, this year the number of issuance fell about 4% to 1,084, implying that the average offering size swelled to roughly $1.7 billion from about $1.4 billion a year ago, thanks to a few jumbo transactions by the largest borrowers.

Hyperscalers Amazon.com and Alphabet top the list of companies that raised the most money by selling bonds this year, the data showed.

Combined with other hyperscalers such as Meta Platforms ( META ) , Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Oracle, it totaled over $370.7 billion, or roughly a fifth of all US investment-grade issuance so far this year, LSEG data showed.

"The market has absorbed the AI issuance and it is evident from the oversubscribed nature of the deals," said Victoria Fernandez, chief market strategist and fixed income portfolio manager at Crossmark Global Investments.

"The AI companies do not seem to be slowing down in coming to both the USD and Euro bond markets."

Apple ( AAPL ) became the latest tech giant to tap the bond market this week. A term sheet seen by Reuters showed the iPhone maker is raising about $7.5 billion from a seven-part US-dollar bond offering.

However, the prospect of higher interest rates is adding to concerns about how quickly massive AI investment will translate into profits and whether heavily indebted companies can generate returns fast enough to service mounting interest costs.

Default insurance costs at some of the biggest AI spenders have surged in recent months. Oracle's five-year spread hit a record 325.45 basis points last month. Amazon ( AMZN ), Alphabet, Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Meta also set records, though well below Oracle's level.

The Democratic sweep in US midterm elections has also sparked concerns about tougher AI regulation and a slowdown in the data-center buildout.

Goldman Sachs analysts flagged delayed AI monetization and growth in purchase commitments as key risks to more debt issuance, according to a note published on Friday.

The bank expects 35% of hyperscalers' capital expenditure to be funded through bond issuance in 2027, roughly in line with the levels seen this year.

(Reporting by Shashwat Chauhan in Bengaluru; Editing by Arun Koyyur)

data.title: TSMC considers making advanced memory chips, The Information reports
data.description:
Nov 6 (Reuters) - Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co ( TSM ) is considering expanding into advanced memory chip production, in a move that would allow it to capture a larger share of the AI hardware market, The Information reported on Friday.

The company recently started charting plans for making a type of advanced memory chips called 3D DRAM at the request of Nvidia ( NVDA ), its biggest customer, the report said, citing two people with direct knowledge of the matter.

TSMC and Nvidia ( NVDA ) did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment.

-- TSMC could opt to build new factories for advanced memory chips, but it was not clear when it plans to begin production, according to the report

-- The world's largest chip manufacturer is also exploring acquiring an existing plant and converting it for memory production, the report said, similar to Micron's move this year to buy a fab and convert it for DRAM output

-- DRAM, or dynamic random access memory, chips are used to store data temporarily in devices. 3D DRAM is a memory architecture that stacks memory cells vertically rather than in a single horizontal layer to boost capacity

-- The push is helmed by Hsu Kuo-chin, a vice president who oversees advanced packaging at TSMC, according to the report

-- TSMC's potential move comes at a time when a severe, AI-driven shortage of memory chips has pushed up prices and sent chip designers scrambling to look for additional supply

-- If TSMC pushes into advanced memory, it will have to compete with companies such as Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron

(Reporting by Deborah Sophia in Bengaluru; Editing by Shilpi Majumdar)

The transaction will strengthen Food Lion’s ability to serve more customers with fresh produce, quality meats, ready-to-eat meals and everyday essentials at affordable prices.

“The addition of these stores will allow us to nourish more families across Georgia,” said Greg Finchum, President, Food Lion. “That is at the heart of who we are at Food Lion. The growth we’re experiencing gives us great momentum as we head into 2027. Each new store broadens our footprint and deepens our presence in the towns and cities we serve, giving our associates the opportunity to offer neighbors the easy and affordable shopping experience they count on from Food Lion.”

  • 3606 Second St. Folkston, Ga. 31537
  • 1060 Lakes Blvd. Lake Park, Ga. 31636
  • 220 Retreat Village St. Simons Island, Ga. 31522

The stores will remain open as Winn-Dixie until the transaction is complete, pending customary closing requirements. data.title: US STOCKS-Nasdaq pares losses as chips recover, rate-hike fears linger
data.description:
* Indexes: Dow down 0.22%, S&P 500 up 1.02%, Nasdaq up 1.82%

* Airbnb ( ABNB ) jumps after raising FY revenue growth forecast

* October nonfarm payrolls at +165,000 vs 65,000 estimate

(Updates to market open)

By Shashwat Chauhan and Utkarsh Hathi

Nov 6 (Reuters) - The tech-heavy Nasdaq rose on Friday as chip stocks bounced off heavy losses posted in the previous session on fears that a Democratic-led Congress could result in tougher AI regulation, even as the jobs report raised interest-rate hike concerns.

The Nasdaq Composite logged its steepest one-day decline in 19 months on Thursday, confirming it had entered correction territory. The index was also headed for a fourth straight weekly fall.

The selloff followed Democrats' midterm election victory, including in some key data-center states, stoking concerns that AI data-center buildout could slow. Optimism over the sector's rapid growth had propelled stock markets to record highs this year.

On Friday, megacap and growth stocks were mixed. Nvidia ( NVDA ) added 6.5%, after suffering its worst day since January 2025 when the emergence of low-cost Chinese AI model DeepSeek rattled Wall Street.

Chip stocks staged a recovery, with broader semiconductor index rising over 6%, after plunging over 12% in the previous session. AMD, Intel ( INTC ), and Micron Technology ( MU ) were up between 7% and 13%.

data.title: October Jobs Growth Tops Forecasts, Raising Odds of December Rate Hike
data.description:
10:33 AM EST, 11/06/2026 (MT Newswires) -- The US economy added more than double the jobs Wall Street expected, boosting the odds for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike next month.

Total nonfarm payrolls rose by 165,000 in October, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said Friday, compared with the 70,000 gain expected in a Bloomberg-compiled survey. The September tally was revised higher by 31,000 to 60,000, while the increase in August was adjusted upwards by 53,000 to 186,000.

The unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1% in October, while the Street expected a stable print of 4.2%.

"This morning's report suggests the labor market is on a slightly stronger footing than previously thought, giving the Fed little reason to remain on the sidelines," said Thomas Feltmate, senior economist at TD Economics.

Markets are now pricing in a 78% probability that the Federal Open Market Committee will raise its benchmark lending rate by 25 basis points in December, up from 67% on Thursday, according to the CME FedWatch tool. The remaining odds favor another pause.

Last month, the FOMC held its benchmark lending rate steady, following a 25-basis-point hike in September to cool stubborn inflation.

Private payrolls increased by 159,000 in October, following a 78,000 rise the month prior, the BLS data showed. The Street expected a gain of 65,000.

The services industry added 144,000 jobs following a 51,000 gain in September. Employment growth slowed in the goods-producing sector as the construction segment swung negative.

"For the Fed, the main message is that the labor market remains strong enough for the committee to retain its primary focus on inflation," Oxford Economics Chief US Economist Michael Pearce said in a note. "We expect another rise in core inflation in October, so the economic data will justify recent calls from policymakers for an additional hike at the December meeting."

The headline personal consumption expenditure price index rose 3.6% year over year in September, following a 3.4% gain the prior month. The core measure -- which excludes the volatile food and energy components -- increased to 3.1% from 3%, official data showed last month.

On Thursday, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said the FOMC may need to continue raising interest rates to curb inflation, though at a gradual pace to minimize economic disruptions. Separately, Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin told CNBC that he expects further rate hikes, but was unsure of the scale and timing.

Last week, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said the FOMC will likely need to tighten monetary policy "soon" to bring inflation down to its 2% goal in a timely manner.

"However, given that most of the inflation overshoot reflects pressures from (artificial intelligence) and spillovers from higher energy prices, the recent sharp declines in tech stocks and global oil prices in anticipation of greater regulation and a negotiated end to the war, respectively, lower the odds of additional hikes in 2027," Oxford's Pearce said.

data.title: Lawyer for Fed's Cook seeks clarity ahead of any White House hearing
data.description:
Nov 6 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook's lawyer has asked the White House to address fairness and process concerns before she attends a hearing that President Donald Trump wants held to assess whether he should fire her, even as one of the conveners said on Friday that it would go forward on December 14 as planned.

Trump has for more than a year been trying to remove Cook over mortgage fraud allegations that she denies and maintains are a pretense to oust her over her monetary policy decisions.

The Supreme Court in June ruled Trump cannot fire a Fed governor "at will" but may be able to do so for cause, if there is an opportunity for a defense. Trump's top economic aide, Kevin Hassett, has said the proposed hearing, which the president initially set for November 5, is designed to provide just that.

A White House official had told Reuters on Wednesday that the hearing had been rescheduled for December 14.

"There are no further changes to the schedule right now," Hassett told Reuters when asked if the White House will proceed with the hearing over objections from Cook's legal team.

Cook's lawyers have said she could be available if certain issues are addressed by the time the hearing is held, including the neutrality of the committee holding it, the "disclosure of any evidence they want to address, and roles of others in the process," a representative for her legal team told Reuters on Thursday, adding that her counsel has asked the White House to resolve those concerns.

Cook's lawyer, Abbe Lowell, had previously raised questions over whether the hearing, part of a White House investigation into Cook to be led by Hassett and two other Trump appointees, would be fair.

(Reporting by Ann Saphir, Bo Erickson and Trevor Hunnicutt; Editing by Jonathan Spicer and Paul Simao)

data.title: Tech employment gains momentum in October, CompTIA analysis finds
data.description:
Tech industry adds 7,200 jobs and IT occupations gain 26,000 as job postings and AI skills demand rise

DOWNERS GROVE, Ill., Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Technology employment and employer demand for tech talent strengthened in October, with gains in industry and occupation employment and continued growth in job postings, according to analysis by CompTIA.

"The strength in tech hiring and job postings is encouraging, but the bigger story is where the demand is occurring."

Tech industry employment increased by approximately 7,200 jobs in October, with gains in manufacturing, information services, search and platforms, and IT and custom software services, according to CompTIA's analysis of U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics data.1

Information technology (IT) occupations throughout the economy increased by approximately 26,000 jobs, while the unemployment rate for IT workers declined to 2.8%, compared with the national unemployment rate of 4.1%.2 More than 7 million people work in tech occupations.

Employers added 290,892 new job postings for IT occupations in October, up 4.5% from September and 22.2% from October 2025. Active job postings totaled 629,876, up 18.5% year over year. From January through October, employers generated approximately 2.66 million new IT occupation job postings, 16.6% more than during the corresponding period in 2025.

"The strength in tech hiring and job postings is encouraging, but the bigger story is where the demand is occurring," said Seth Robinson, vice president, research, CompTIA. "Employers across industries are looking for people with software, AI, cybersecurity, data, systems and networking capabilities, reinforcing the value of building adaptable technology skills."

Demand grows for core tech roles and AI skills

Software developer and engineer positions led the market with 51,944 new postings in October, up 6.3% from September. Several occupations posted double-digit gains, including DevOps engineers, infrastructure architects, cybersecurity engineers and data scientists.

Active job postings associated with AI skills reached 366,322, up 6.2% from September. Demand for specialized AI positions increased 9.8%. The two measures illustrate the different dimensions of AI workforce demand. AI-specific job titles represent specialized roles, while the expanded skills measure captures broader employer demand for AI capabilities across jobs that may not carry an AI-specific title.

Employers across professional and technical services, manufacturing, health care, construction and other sectors continue to seek workers with technology skills, underscoring the economy-wide nature of tech talent demand.

data.title: TSMC considers making advanced memory chips, The Information reports
data.description:
Nov 6 (Reuters) - Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co ( TSM ) is considering expanding into advanced memory chip production, in a move that would allow it to capture a larger share of the AI hardware market, The Information reported on Friday.

The company recently started charting plans for making a type of advanced memory chips called 3D DRAM at the request of Nvidia ( NVDA ), its biggest customer, the report said, citing two people with direct knowledge of the matter.

TSMC and Nvidia ( NVDA ) did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment.

* TSMC could opt to build new factories for advanced memory chips, but it was not clear when it plans to begin production, according to the report

* The world's largest chip manufacturer is also exploring acquiring an existing plant and converting it for memory production, the report said, similar to Micron's move this year to buy a fab and convert it for DRAM output

* DRAM, or dynamic random access memory, chips are used to store data temporarily in devices. 3D DRAM is a memory architecture that stacks memory cells vertically rather than in a single horizontal layer to boost capacity

* The push is helmed by Hsu Kuo-chin, a vice president who oversees advanced packaging at TSMC, according to the report

* TSMC's potential move comes at a time when a severe, AI-driven shortage of memory chips has pushed up prices and sent chip designers scrambling to look for additional supply

* If TSMC pushes into advanced memory, it will have to compete with companies such as Samsung Electronics ( SSNLF ), SK Hynix ( SKHY ) and Micron

data.title: Exclusive-Apple's autocomplete restrictions include 'Dictator Trump' and 'Sleepy Joe,' researcher finds
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 6 (Reuters) - Apple has an undisclosed multilingual gray list of tens of thousands of words and phrases that its iOS keyboard will not autocomplete or swipe-type, a researcher said on Friday.

The list is not a ban. iPhone users can still type what they like when drafting emails and texts. But the words on the list will not be suggested to users via autocomplete or swipe-typing in most cases. The researcher, Derek Kauffman, said the find opens a window into how Apple manages the tradeoff between anticipating what hundreds of millions of iPhone users are trying to say and preventing the devices from offering offensive or politically charged suggestions to users - something he said could quietly shape how they communicate. 

"It's a very light-touch form of censorship," said Kauffman said. "But at the scale that Apple is operating, it only takes a light touch to have a big impact."

Most of the flagged words and phrases are vulgar, offensive or related to drugs, sex or violence, according to Kauffman, who discovered the list recently and has published a website itemizing them. But some are politically charged, including "dictator Trump" and "sleepy Joe."

In an email, Apple did not comment directly on Kauffman's findings, including the size or composition of its list, or its reasons for flagging certain political terms. It said that iPhone users always had the option to type specific words or phrases and could always override any predictive text suggestions. Apple said its keyboard was set up to avoid offering suggestions that might be inappropriate or offensive.

Other phrases excluded from iOS's predictive text features include "right wing conspiracy" as well as "Tibetan independence" and "United Ireland," according to Kauffman. Non-English languages have different flagged words or phrases. In Hindi, for example, the keyboard does not allow users to swipe-type "Modi braggart" or "Rahul is Pappu," digs at India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his leading opponent,  Rahul Gandhi, respectively, according to Kauffman.

He said French speakers could not swipe-type the French phrase "immigration too high" and that Hebrew speakers could not swipe-type "occupied territories."

"Every major language has some version of this," Kauffman said.

Kauffman said it was understandable that Apple wanted to keep users from accidentally sending obscene messages or inflammatory slogans. But he said there were inconsistencies in how Apple applied the feature. For example, he said "read smut" could be swipe-typed while "read gay smut" could not.

HOW THE GRAY LIST WAS DISCOVERED

Kauffman said he found the list in September after noticing that his swipe-typing - the practice of gliding a finger back and forth over a keyboard rather than pecking out each word individually - would stutter over certain phrases, like "bad boy" or "white man," but not "bad girl" or "black man." 

His curiosity piqued, Kauffman said he used a combination of OpenAI's Codex and Anthropic's Claude Code to hunt for a reason why, eventually stumbling on a compendium stored "deep in the bowels" of Apple's operating system. He said there were different ways to count the number of gray-listed words and phrases and their various permutations, but a conservative estimate would put them at about 100,000, not including Chinese characters.

Reuters tested a small subset of the phrases identified by Kauffman on an iPhone and found they were all difficult to enter through swipe-typing or were not suggested via autocomplete. Attempts to swipe-type "United Ireland" or "Tibetan independence" often yielded "United Iceland" or "Tibetan independences," for example. Trying to swipe-type "white man" would yield "white mean," while "red man" or "blue man" could be swipe-typed without difficulty. "Sleepy Joe" would yield "Sleepy hope." "Dictator Trump" could be swipe-typed, but "trump" was lowercase and the phrase was not suggested in autocomplete - the keyboard instead suggested "dictator trumps." Swipe-typing "read gay smut" would yield "Read gay Smit." "Read smut" could be swipe-typed with no issue.

Matt Suiche, an engineer at agentic AI cybersecurity company Tolmo, said he was able to independently recover the same gray list and cross-reference Kauffman's findings against Apple's internal data. He said he got a near-perfect match.

Suiche said the Apple list had been hidden in plain sight for years, providing an interesting look at how "human communication has been potentially influenced and filtered for years inside messaging apps."

A CALL FOR TRANSPARENCY   

Kauffman is not alone in having picked up on the nudges from iOS's predictive text feature. Over the years, social media users have wondered why they could not swipe-type certain phrases. Earlier this week, a Norwegian systems administrator independently discovered a list of words on Apple's gray list, including "al-Qaeda," "Auschwitz" and "Hooters," but the existence of a wider list of sensitive phrases is reported here for the first time.

Apple, like other tech companies, has previously run into trouble when predictive technology suggests embarrassing or controversial texts to users. Alphabet-owned Google's autocomplete feature has regularly attracted criticism - and sometimes even litigation - over its suggested search terms. Last year, Apple drew media attention when users reported that dictating the word "racist" to their iPhones would briefly cause the word "Trump" to flash across their screens. Apple said at the time that the problem was an error and had been fixed.

David Greene, the senior counsel at the Electronic Frontier Foundation, a digital civil liberties group, said that while a part of him found the word list "creepy" and he wondered about Apple's judgment calls, he could see an argument for it being a useful way to curb unwanted or inflammatory suggestions. 

"But if they are going to do it, this is something users should be really well aware of and have some ability to customize," Greene said. "This is something that should not be secret."

(Reporting by Raphael Satter in Washington; Editing by Matthew Lewis)
